_comment: Semantic versions for the hand-written player-facing content that documents
the game: the instruction booklet and the /play load-screen cards.
WHAT THIS CONTENT TARGETS (owner, 2026-09-08): the EPISODE ONE DESIGN — the
game as it is meant to behave — NOT the build that happens to be deployed.
The booklet is closer to a spec than to release notes, and the game catches up
to it. This may change once Episode One is finished; for now the design is the
target.
That inverts the staleness question. The useful signal is not 'is the manual
behind the game' but 'what has the game not caught up with yet' — which is a
known, temporary, expected state, and a to-do for the game rather than a
defect in the book. aheadOfLive is that list.
It also means a documented behaviour that is not live is CORRECT, not wrong.
The trap it creates is the opposite one: finding the game doing something the
booklet does not say and 'fixing' the booklet to match. Arc flagged exactly
that with the Health Relic — its +25% maxHP does nothing on equip today, and
the booklet would have been wrong to describe the bug. Check whether a
difference is a game defect before treating it as a documentation error.
WHY SEMVER AND NOT A GIT SHA: a hash tells you which build shipped, but two
hashes cannot be compared — you cannot look at ec589de and 146964d and say
which is newer. Version numbers sort.
BUMP RULES (version):
major - restructured (chapters added/removed/reordered)
minor - a mechanic's description changed, or content was added
patch - wording, typos, a figure swap; nothing a player learns differently
reviewed  - when a person last read this against the design.
history   - append-only; the game version at each content version, which
answers 'what was the game when the manual was X'. Newest first.

history.note: Retargeted at the Episode One design rather than the deployed build. Interrupt now costs the whole turn; statuses tick at end of turn (which removes the last-stack-acts-free behaviour entirely); the winding-up hint now states the payoff.

Initiative trigger corrected, turn economy added, status-stacking model rewritten, combat log expanded with its figure, controller + battle speed added, Mother Slime reach 1→2, auto-save indicator, Cure vs Mugwort.
Pre-review baseline: the booklet as it stood when the 0.8.2592 delta review began. Recorded retrospectively; earlier history predates versioning.

aheadOfLive.item: Interrupt applies Stunned — the creature loses its next turn, not just its reactions
Statuses tick and decrement at the END of the affected unit's turn (was the start)
Status stacks make the same status easier to land again (QB-116)

history.note: Winding-up-enemy card now states the payoff (a free turn) rather than arguing from what retreating costs.

Rewritten as short snippets from the booklet's Hints chapter. AP removed — it had been retired from the game while three cards still taught it. Cut to Episode One content. Cure corrected against Mugwort.

aheadOfLive.item: Breaking a charge costs the enemy its next turn
